steps.content: Starting with a Random Forest model to establish a baseline accuracy. Using 100 trees should provide a strong ensemble, and setting max_depth to 10 may help control overfitting.

The Random Forest model with 100 trees and a max depth of 10 achieved a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.95978, which is promising. The validation accuracy was slightly lower at 0.95322. This configuration is stable with a standard deviation of 0.01476. I will continue to explore variations around this configuration.
Testing a higher number of trees (200) with the same max depth to see if the ensemble can be improved further. More trees may enhance performance without overfitting due to the controlled depth.

The Random Forest model with 200 trees and a max depth of 10 maintained the same mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.95978 and validation accuracy of 0.95322 as the previous configuration. There is no improvement, so I will try adjusting the max depth to see if it can enhance performance.
Reducing the max depth to 8 might increase the model's ability to generalize by preventing overfitting while still leveraging a substantial number of trees (200).

The Random Forest model with 200 trees and a max depth of 8 did not improve the mean cross-validated accuracy or validation accuracy, which remain at 0.95978 and 0.95322, respectively. Since there is no improvement, I will switch to exploring the Gradient Boosting model for potential better results.

Starting with a Gradient Boosting model to explore its performance. Using 100 estimators and a max depth of 3 as a balanced configuration to prevent overfitting while allowing for sufficient complexity.

The Gradient Boosting model with 100 estimators and a max depth of 3 achieved a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.94475, which is lower than the best Random Forest configuration. The validation accuracy of 0.93567 also reflects this. I will continue to optimize the Gradient Boosting model by adjusting the number of estimators.
Increasing the number of estimators to 200 for the Gradient Boosting model may enhance accuracy by allowing for more boosting iterations, potentially leading to better performance.

The Gradient Boosting model with 200 estimators and a max depth of 3 resulted in a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.94218 and a validation accuracy of 0.94152, both of which are still below the best Random Forest configuration. Since there is no improvement, I will explore adjusting the max depth for further optimization.
Increasing the max depth to 4 for the Gradient Boosting model may allow for more complex decision boundaries, potentially improving accuracy.

The Gradient Boosting model with 200 estimators and a max depth of 4 resulted in a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.92715 and a validation accuracy of 0.91813, both of which are lower than previous configurations. This indicates that increasing the max depth has negatively impacted performance. Given that all configurations tested thus far have not surpassed the best Random Forest model, I will stop here and recommend the best Random Forest configuration.

steps.final_recommendation: Random Forest with n_estimators=100 and max_depth=10, as it achieved the highest mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.95978.
